security_spec.violation_condition: When QEMU TCG translates any signed averaging subtract instruction (PASUB.B, PASUB.H, PASUB.W, ASUB, PASUB.DB, PASUB.DH, PASUB.DW) and uses a logical right shift (tcg_gen_shri_*) instead of an arithmetic right shift (tcg_gen_sari_*) on the intermediate subtraction result, negative results lose sign extension — the MSB of each lane is filled with 0 instead of 1, violating the spec requirement 'shifts right by 1 (toward negative infinity)'. Similarly, for unsigned variants (PASUBU.*, ASUBU), if the subtraction is performed at the operand bit-width (e.g., 8-bit for .B) rather than at full precision (e.g., 9-bit for .B), a wrapped unsigned result is shifted instead of the true mathematical difference, producing incorrect lane values.
security_spec.summary: Signed averaging subtract instructions require arithmetic (sign-extending) right shift per spec 'toward negative infinity'; unsigned variants require subtraction at wider-than-operand precision before shift — using logical shift for signed or operand-width subtraction for unsigned produces silently wrong lane results, corrupting guest SIMD computation output

findings.finding: Signed averaging subtract for .B/.H/.W lanes: subtraction widened to int64_t before computing (int64_t)a - b, so the intermediate result is at full 65-bit mathematical precision. The right shift (res >> 1) on the signed int64_t is an arithmetic shift, correctly rounding toward negative infinity per the spec.

Signed averaging subtract for .D lanes: cannot widen beyond int64_t, so manual overflow detection is used. (res ^ a) & (a ^ b) & INT64_MIN captures when bit 64 would differ from bit 63, and XORing it into the shifted result reconstructs the correct sign-extended value. Correctly rounds toward negative infinity.

Unsigned averaging subtract for .B/.H/.W lanes: operands widened to int64_t via (int64_t)a - b, producing the exact signed mathematical difference at full precision. The arithmetic right shift on the result is correct for all cases including when a < b (negative difference).

Unsigned averaging subtract for .D lanes: uses borrow detection (res > a) to reconstruct the 65th bit (bit 64 = !borrow), then ORs it into the logical right shift result. This correctly computes (a - b) >> 1 with full precision, equivalent to widening to 65-bit before shifting.

Translation layer correctly delegates to OPIVV/OPIVX helpers with vxrm rounding mode support. No raw TCG shift operations are used inline — all arithmetic is in the helper functions (asub32/asub64/asubu32/asubu64 in vector_helper.c).

findings.finding: Instruction decoding: vasub_vv and vasub_vx use funct6=001011 (signed averaging subtract), vasubu_vv and vasubu_vx use funct6=001010 (unsigned averaging subtract). Both correctly distinguished from the vaadd/vaaddu encodings (001001/001000) and from vsadd/vssub by the funct6 bits. No aliasing with P-ext opcodes since P-ext is not yet implemented.
